findings: A. FORGED SAVE: reproducible in full. 42/42 places, 42846/42846 cells, 42 squares drawn, nothing dropped. The round-1 W1-21 outcome, via a new route: forge `stood` instead of `places`. Shot: docs/shots/2026-08-08-critic-map-forged.png

A. THE INSTRUMENT CANNOT NOTICE. restore() COMPUTES phantom_cells/missing_cells/stood_cells/legacy; save/state.js:674 keeps only .dropped; mapState() and getUIState().map publish no footprint field. map-probe L3 forges world.discovery.places - the field RESTORE_READS deliberately EXCLUDES - so it cannot fail for the case that matters, and none of the three --break self-tests touches the forgery path.

A. THE TREE CONTRADICTS ITSELF: discovery.js's header claims the map fails closed against a blob whose every field is attacker-controlled; tools/harness/w1-21-r2-forge.mjs R8 asserts an all-ones footprint yields every place and calls it a recorded limit. R8 is right. The header is what the next author will read.

PROVENANCE: game/src/sim/discovery.js was rewritten at 23:32:58 on 2026-08-07 by W1-21-r2 (still in_progress), AFTER W1-MAP recorded itself complete. The footprint wire format changed from a raw bitset to a zigzag-varint delta trail. MY FIRST FORGERY USED THE FORMAT THE W1-MAP STATUS FILE DESCRIBES AND DECODED TO NOTHING - it read exactly like a successful defence. Check Afmt now proves the attack is delivered before any A-result is believed. Any critic re-running this must do the same.

B. REACHABLE ROUTE, EXECUTED: sim.discovery is writable+configurable and QuestEngine holds the sim (engine.js:526, machine.js:79). Substituting the model drew 3 squares. Path: sim.discovery = X -> Engine._uiCtx() engine.js:3448 -> _mapModel -> drawMap. api.js:272 declares this 'not defended' and declines to run it; I ran it. One line closes it.

B. The quest tree itself is CLEAN: grep over game/src/sim/quest/ for map|discovery|__ENGINE|reveal finds only quest-internal reveal() knowledge flags, one S35 comment and the marker-phrase regex. No quest module reaches a map module.

C. UNRENDERED HOLDS, verified at the framebuffer: an empty map is exactly ONE colour with 0 cells drawn. CAUTION FOR SUCCESSORS: a naive pixel sample counts 15 colours on that same blank map, entirely from the player chevron's antialiased edge. Exclude the chevron rect or you will invent a finding.

D. HOLDS: square appears only after standing in the pad (region +480m false, near +40m false, standing true); the hover name is the pois.json name; the naming element carries quest:null objective:null travel:false.

E. Builder's claims CONFIRMED: map-probe 32/32, --break all gives three genuine SELF-TEST OK. Good instrument, and it caught real bugs. Its gap is L3, which is aimed at a field the loader never reads.

F. CONSUMPTION: NO world-side consumer. Nothing under game/src/sim/ reads sim.discovery. Ablation with the discovery blob excluded from the hash gives an IDENTICAL world hash (5094c15a:442141) in both arms. The only consumer is the map's own draw call.

FOREIGN DEFECT, not the map's: combat/enemy.js:303 _idleBehaviour throws 'this.ai.step is not a function' inside the fixed step on some routes. critic-w1-map-stepcheck.mjs reproduces it with sim.discovery removed entirely. It first presented as four map-shaped failures (C2, D1, D2, D3) that were really a walk whose steps never ran; C0 and D0 now assert per-block that the world stepped.

MY OWN SELF-TESTS EACH FAILED FIRST AND HAD TO BE REPAIRED: --break standing asserted seenAt(site), but the reveal radius at Thorn is 40 m so a body 480 m away revealed nothing and the break never fired; --break consumer perturbed stamina, which regenerates before the hash is taken. Both were passing for the wrong reason.
